Orlen stock reshapes LNG portfolio after QatarEnergy contract ends
sum: Orlen is ending one of its two long-term liquefied natural gas supply agreements with QatarEnergy after months of disrupted deliveries. The Polish energy group exercised its termination right on Tuesday, November 10, citing continuing force majeure and an inability to meet contractual delivery obligations, according to Purely Energy.

The terminated agreement covered 1 million metric tons of LNG per year and was scheduled to run until 2034. The contract will remain in force for 60 days after the termination notice. Its pricing formula was linked to crude oil quotations, which has become less attractive as alternative LNG supply arrangements develop.

The decision affects only one of Orlen's two long-term QatarEnergy agreements. The second contract covers up to 1 million metric tons of LNG annually through 2034 and is linked to gas-market benchmarks rather than crude oil prices. That arrangement remains in place.

QatarEnergy declared force majeure in March after disruption at LNG facilities in Ras Laffan and interruptions to tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Orlen had previously expected Qatari deliveries to resume in mid-November, but the continuing supply disruption led to the termination decision.

Orlen says the change will not threaten the security of its gas supply. The group points to production from its own fields, other long-term agreements and deliveries from the United States. A separate long-term offtake arrangement with Venture Global's Plaquemines facility in Louisiana has also started supplying Orlen.

For investors, the termination shifts attention from the lost volume to the economics and resilience of Orlen's broader gas portfolio. Ending an oil-linked agreement can reduce exposure to a contract that has become commercially less attractive, while retaining the gas-linked QatarEnergy deal preserves access to a major LNG supplier. The 60-day notice period leaves a defined transition phase rather than an immediate removal of the agreement.

The move also highlights the balance between supply security and procurement flexibility. Orlen retains Norwegian production, US supply and its remaining Qatari contract, but future returns will depend on the cost and availability of replacement cargoes as well as the terms of its long-term commitments.

Orlen Terminates Long-Term LNG Contract With QatarEnergy Citing Force Majeure
sum: Orlen, the Polish energy group listed in Warsaw, has terminated one of its two long-term liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply contracts with QatarEnergy. The group cites persistent force majeure that has resulted in no deliveries. The contract remains in force during a notice period, and its effective end comes only when that period expires. On the market, other suppliers are signing new contracts, as shown by TotalEnergies' agreement with Jiangsu Guoxin.

The terminated contract is the older of the two. Polskie Górnictwo Naftowe i Gazownictwo (PGNiG), the former gas group whose rights Orlen now exercises, signed it while Poland was preparing its first regasification terminal to diversify its gas sources. Deliveries began later than the original schedule. According to Orlen, the price of the terminated contract is indexed to oil quotations, while the second contract with QatarEnergy, which is still being performed, is indexed to gas quotations. The exact pricing formulas are not public.

In its stock exchange filing, Orlen states that the decision does not affect the group's gas supply security. According to the company, its own production and its other long-term contracts cover all of its needs. No independent source confirms this claim. Orlen is also a customer of Venture Global, whose Plaquemines plant in the United States is among its supply sources, while Italy is preparing a reference threshold on gas costs for power plants.

Force majeure is a clause that releases a seller from its delivery obligations when an external event prevents it from performing the contract. It suspends deliveries without penalty for as long as it lasts, but does not terminate the contract. QatarEnergy halted its LNG production following military attacks targeting its industrial sites, then declared force majeure to the buyers concerned. Orlen received its own notification shortly afterwards.

Subsequent missile strikes damaged two liquefaction trains, a significant share of Qatar's export capacity, and the announced repair time has varied according to the statements. All Qatari exports pass through the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic has been severely disrupted. QatarEnergy has renewed its force majeure notifications many times, including recently for other European buyers.

items.t: Orlen stock ends Qatar LNG deal as force majeure halts deliveries
sum: Orlen said on Tuesday, November 10, that it had terminated one of its two long-term liquefied natural gas agreements with QatarEnergy after prolonged force majeure prevented deliveries. The decision changes the Polish energy group's supply mix while leaving a second QatarEnergy contract in place.

The Polish Press Agency PAP reported that the terminated agreement was signed in 2009 by Polish Oil and Gas Company, now part of Orlen. It covered annual deliveries of 1 million tonnes of LNG, equivalent to approximately 15.3 TWh, and was scheduled to run until 2034. Orlen estimated its 2026 value at EUR 570 million.

The terminated agreement will remain in force for another 60 days after the notice. Orlen's separate QatarEnergy contract covers up to 1 million tonnes per year under a formula linked to gas-market prices and remains valid through 2034.

Orlen said the termination does not threaten gas security. The group pointed to its own production and existing long-term supply agreements as sufficient to cover demand. For investors, the move removes one disrupted supply arrangement but keeps QatarEnergy exposure through the second contract.
Orlen stock traded at 28.89 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:10 CET on Wednesday, November 11.

Orlen stock: Q3 cash flow supports PLN 7.8 billion investment
sum: ORLEN's third-quarter results, released on Thursday, November 5, put cash generation and capital allocation at the center of the investment case. In its quarterly release, the group reported revenue of PLN 80.1 billion, LIFO-based EBITDA of PLN 14.8 billion and net profit of PLN 5.6 billion.
Orlen stock traded at 28.93 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:14 CET on Tuesday, November 10.

Operating cash flow reached PLN 12.8 billion in the quarter, while ORLEN invested PLN 7.8 billion in growth projects. The company said the spending is aimed at energy security and expansion across Poland and the wider region.

The operating mix remains important for investors. Upstream & Supply generated EBITDA of PLN 4.7 billion, while Downstream delivered LIFO-based EBITDA of PLN 6.3 billion on refinery crude throughput of 10.1 million tonnes. Energy generated EBITDA of PLN 2.7 billion, supported by a nearly 30% year-on-year increase in renewable electricity generation.

ORLEN is expanding its resource base while securing feedstock for its refineries. The company said an October appraisal more than doubled its share of recoverable gas at the Afrodite field to above 4 billion cubic metres. A three-year Equinor supply agreement could provide more than 9 million tonnes of crude annually, covering up to a quarter of the group's requirements.

The Baltic Power offshore wind farm has entered commissioning and testing after turbine installation was completed. For investors, the results therefore combine near-term sensitivity to refining conditions with a broad investment program whose returns will depend on execution, energy prices and commodity markets.
The Polish equity-market backdrop is covered in the WIG 20 market overview.

The results leave investors balancing earnings pressure against the group's broader operating base. Cash generation, spending on energy infrastructure and the delivery of transition projects will shape how the market assesses the quarter.

The earnings miss also raises the importance of refining conditions in the next reporting cycle. Energy, renewables and international operations provide diversification, but they do not remove the sensitivity to margins, commodity markets and execution risk.

ORLEN's near-term priorities are the conversion of its investment program into operating returns, the development of gas resources and the performance of refining and fuel markets. The latest quarterly figures give investors a new benchmark for those factors rather than a standalone signal on future share-price direction.

Poland’s biggest corporate taxpayers
sum: Who pays tax on corporate profits in Poland? Which companies were the largest corporate income taxpayers in their industries? The 462 companies with tax bills above PLN 20m contributed PLN 47.5bn to the budget for 2025, up 22% from a year earlier. PKO BP topped the list again, just ahead of Orlen, while banks took five of the top 10 places. Here is the ranking prepared by XYZ.

As we did last year, we examined who pays the most corporate income tax, or CIT, in Poland. We recognized the largest taxpayers across the economy and in individual industries at a special 2025 Largest CIT Taxpayers Gala. The awards were presented by Andrzej Domański, minister of finance and economy.

Our CIT ranking is based on 2025 taxpayer data published by the Ministry of Finance. We first combined the databases of individual CIT taxpayers and tax capital groups. We then ranked these entities by the amount of CIT due, producing a list of the 10 largest taxpayers in 2025.
We subsequently assigned every entity with more than PLN 20m in tax due to an industry. On that basis, we identified the largest CIT taxpayers in 27 sectors.
XYZ analysis based on Ministry of Finance data. CIT for 2025.
In addition to the 27 industry leaders, we recognized the 10 largest CIT taxpayers overall.

As in the previous year, banks dominated the list, taking five of the top 10 places, including two on the podium. The largest taxpayer was PKO Bank Polski — more precisely, the PKO BP tax capital group — which paid PLN 3bn in CIT for 2025. Orlen followed closely, with tax due of around PLN 2.95bn. Third place went to Erste Bank Polska, which operated as Santander Bank Polska until April 2026 and paid PLN 2.45bn.

items.t: Orlen stock weighs Q3 pressure as LNG expansion advances
sum: ORLEN's third-quarter results put operating resilience and refining pressure at the center of the week's investor focus. The company's financial presentation, released on Thursday, November 5, showed PLN 80.1 billion in revenue and PLN 14.8 billion in EBITDA LIFO for the quarter. ORLEN stock traded at 29.82 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:35 CET on Saturday, November 7. The real-time quote of Orlen stock is available separately.

Operating cash flow reached PLN 12.7 billion, while capital expenditure stood at PLN 7.8 billion. Net debt to EBITDA was -0.06x, underlining the group's reported balance-sheet position after the quarter.

Segment results were uneven. Downstream EBITDA LIFO was PLN 6.3 billion, Upstream & Supply contributed PLN 4.7 billion, Energy generated PLN 2.7 billion and Consumers & Products delivered PLN 1.5 billion. The presentation also showed crude oil throughput of 10.1 million tonnes and hydrocarbon production of 16.8 million barrels of oil equivalent.

ORLEN said on October 27 that it plans to open a Singapore LNG trading office in the first quarter of 2027. The office will operate within ORLEN LNG Trading and is intended to strengthen customer relationships in Asia while extending trading coverage across European and Asian time zones. The company also said LNG deliveries from the Plaquemines terminal under its Venture Global contract would begin in early November.

The Singapore plan gives investors a longer-term strategic theme alongside the quarterly figures. Its commercial contribution will depend on cargo availability, trading conditions and the group's ability to optimise its expanding LNG carrier fleet.

European energy investors will continue to weigh refining margins, energy-market conditions and ORLEN's investment programme. Current Euro Stoxx 50 market reports provide the broader regional context.

sum: ORLEN is approaching its third-quarter reporting date with investors focused on the gap between expectations and the final figures. Portevo updated its English earnings page on Tuesday, November 3, and lists Thursday, November 5, 2026, as the next report date.

The page puts the consensus EPS estimate for the current quarter at PLN 6.08 and expected revenue at PLN 76.70 billion. The forecast comes from one analyst, making the figures a narrow reference point rather than a broad market consensus. The upcoming release will show whether ORLEN can sustain the stronger profitability recorded in the previous quarter.

ORLEN's latest reported quarter ended June 30, 2026. Revenue reached PLN 76.47 billion and net income was PLN 7.68 billion, according to the Portevo summary. EPS came in at PLN 6.66 against a forecast of PLN 5.32, a 25.23 percent beat.

The previous result also illustrates why the headline earnings number may not determine the immediate share response. Portevo says ORLEN stock fell 0.76 percent in the first session after that release, despite the earnings beat. Across the last four reports, results exceeded forecasts in half of the quarters, while the average first-session move was 1.54 percent in either direction.

For investors, the central question is whether the November 5 report confirms the earnings improvement implied by the forecast or exposes pressure in the group's operating businesses. The report is likely to be assessed against both the expected EPS and the prior quarter's revenue and profit base. Historical reactions suggest that even a positive surprise may not translate into a straightforward share-price gain.

Orlen stock faces impairment review ahead of November 5 results
sum: ORLEN's third-quarter update combines a material accounting charge with mixed operating trends ahead of the group's results on Thursday, November 5, 2026. In a regulatory announcement published by Parkiet, the company said on October 22 that it expects impairment charges in its consolidated third-quarter 2026 accounts.

ORLEN anticipates PLN 1.6 billion of impairment charges. The gross items include PLN 1.6 billion in Downstream, mainly linked to spending on the New Chemistry project, and PLN 0.8 billion in Energy. The group also expects to reverse PLN 0.8 billion of earlier impairments in Upstream & Supply.

The charges are non-cash and do not directly affect operating cash flow for the current reporting period. They can nevertheless reduce reported earnings and asset values, leaving the statutory auditor's review and the final consolidated accounts as important checkpoints for investors.

Third-quarter crude oil, condensate and natural gas liquids production fell to 4,285 thousand barrels of oil equivalent from 4,633 thousand a year earlier. Natural gas production declined to 21.6 terawatt-hours from 23.3 terawatt-hours, while gas imports into Poland dropped to 39.4 terawatt-hours from 54.0 terawatt-hours.

Other indicators were more resilient. Electricity generation rose to 4.0 terawatt-hours from 3.7 terawatt-hours, and retail electricity sales increased to 4.1 terawatt-hours from 3.7 terawatt-hours. Crude processing reached 10,083 thousand tonnes, 1 percent below the year-earlier level, while refinery utilization matched the prior-year quarter at 94 percent.

Orlen stock traded at 32.65 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 3:35 p.m. CET on Monday, November 2, 2026; that was 2.71 percent below the 33.56-euro quote in the October 30 report. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Orlen stock.

sum: Simply Wall St raised its fair value for Orlen from PLN 154.03 to PLN 156.39 on October 16, 2026, putting valuation back at the center of the stock discussion. The change came as the research narrative placed greater weight on low-emission projects, capital discipline and foreign energy operations. Orlen stock was trading at EUR 35.25 at Lang & Schwarz on October 21, 2026, at 3:40 p.m. CEST.

The updated fair value represents a 1.53 percent increase from PLN 154.03. Simply Wall St also reported that the future price-to-earnings multiple moved from 12.92 to 13.12, while its valuation model retained a 9.66 percent discount rate.

The research update identified a PLN 16.00 billion budget reduction for Orlen's New Chemicals project as a factor that could influence future capital intensity and net margins. It also highlighted the company's low and zero-emission project pipeline and combined-cycle gas turbine plants.

Orlen generated PLN 152.20 billion revenue in the first half of 2026, an increase of PLN 17.80 billion from the same period a year earlier. Net profit reached PLN 15.90 billion, while EBITDA stood at PLN 28.70 billion, according to the Q2 2026 earnings summary published by Quartr.

Second-quarter revenue was PLN 76.50 billion and net profit was PLN 7.70 billion. Operating cash flow reached PLN 15.20 billion in the quarter, while capital expenditure was PLN 9.30 billion. The figures show why the valuation debate extends beyond refining margins and includes investment intensity and cash generation.

Orlen's next earnings date is November 5, 2026, for third-quarter results, as listed by Quartr. The company operates across refining, petrochemicals, energy, retail and upstream activities, giving the result a broad operational base.

For investors, the key comparison is between the PLN 156.39 fair value and the company's capital program. The October 16 update raised the valuation modestly, but its own assumptions still place capital discipline and project execution alongside earnings growth.

Poland detains five current and former Orlen staff over fuel pricing
sum: The Polish Internal Security Agency (ABW) has detained five current and former managers of Poland's energy giant Orlen over the unjustified lowering of fuel prices between August and November 2023, the National Prosecutor's Office (PK) said on Tuesday.
The detentions took place on Monday, the PK said in a post on X, adding that the detainees include one former member of the management board who served between 2018 and 2024.
"The prosecutor presented charges to all detainees in an investigation ongoing for over two years...," the PK added. "Procedural activities are continuing."
Later on Tuesday, Justice Minister and Prosecutor General Waldemar Zurek commented on the ongoing probe on X.

"In autumn 2023, Daniel 'I can do anything' Obajtek [former Orlen CEO] micromanaged prices at filling stations," he wrote. "Suppressing fuel prices against market logic right before the election and brazenly telling Poles that dry pumps were caused by 'dispenser breakdowns' was no economic miracle," he added.
Zurek called it "an act of asset stripping against the state", designed solely to keep the former ruling socially conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party in power. (PAP)

Orlen opens its first German EV charging hub
sum: Multinational energy corporation Orlen has opened its first multi-bay fast-charging hub for EVs in Germany.
The new EV charging hub consists of 16 400kW chargers and is located on the A23 motorway near Hamburg. The site also features a solar PV canopy to supply it with renewable energy.

Orlen commissioned its first EV charging hub, through its Orlen Charge brand, in its home country of Poland in November 2025. That was part of a larger strategy announced at the same time to open 12 such sites in Poland. The Polish hubs are deployed as part of the “Perun E-mobility” project, co-financed by the European Union under the CEF Transport AFIF instrument.

It specified that all of its fast-charging EV hubs will feature between six and 12 chargepoints capable of delivering up to 400kW, and an intelligent power-sharing system to automatically allocate power between connected vehicles, ensuring that each receives the optimal charging rate.
The hubs are intended to enable EVs to charge within 20 minutes, comparable to the time drivers would spend at a motorway rest point to refuel an internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle.

Although the charging hubs are a new initiative for the company, Orlen has been operating EV chargers across several European markets under the Orlen Charge brand and others owned by the Orlen Group, like Energa.

Collectively, it has over 1,200 chargepoints operating in Poland and 220 in Germany. Orlen is targeting a 33% EV charging market share in Poland by 2030, which would be about 6,000 chargers, and 2,500 chargepoints in other central European markets by the same point.

items.t: Polish government approves windfall tax on fuel firms’ excess profits
sum: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!

Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.

Poland’s government has approved a one-off tax on excess profits earned by fuel companies following a surge in energy prices triggered by the war in Iran. State energy giant Orlen is expected to bear the bulk of the levy.

The proposed tax, which still requires parliamentary approval and the signature of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki, would apply to profits generated between March and December 2026. The government expects the measure to raise around 4 billion zloty (€940 million).
Dzisiaj podejmiemy decyzję o podatku od nadzwyczajnych zysków. Firmy w dużej mierze sfinansują koszt akcji CPN, same na tym nie stracą, ale też nie zarobią. pic.twitter.com/Gtb8eDVJPI

Under the draft law, which was approved by the cabinet on Tuesday, excess profits would be defined as revenue from liquid fuel sales exceeding the amount that would have been generated using a company’s average 2025 fuel sales margin, increased by 20%. Such windfall gains would be taxed at a rate of 60%.

Announcing the plans, the finance ministry said the levy was intended as a response to “exceptional economic and geopolitical conditions that have led to above-average financial results in a specific segment of the fuel sector, not resulting from improved operational efficiency…but from a supply shock.”

items.t: Angelicoussis’ MGM LNG carrier newbuild pair under long-term charter to Orlen
sum: Angelicoussis’ Maran Gas Maritime newbuild LNG carriers were delivered to Poland’s Orlen under long-term charters.
Greek Maran Gas Maritime is expanding its fleet with two more South Korean newbuildings. The company shared a photo in the social media of the delivery of the pair from Hanwha Ocean.

The Greek shipowner didn’t disclose any financial details about the order, but it said that Danuta Siedzikowna – Inka and Rotmistrz Witold Pilecki, are the fifth and sixth vessels of a series of thirteen LNG carriers ordered by Maran Gas Maritime to Hanwha Ocean, with slated deliveries within April 2026.

With a cargo capacity of 174,000 cubic meters, the vessels’ design includes a hull form optimized for a wider range of trading speeds, an efficient ME-GI propulsion plant, shaft generators for onboard power generation, and an air lubrication system to further enhance vessels’ performance.

“This specification has significant advantages over currently competing designs,” the Greek company said. “It includes lower consumptions and negligible level of methane slip which yield to the lowest environmental footprint among all LNG vessels currently in the market,” it added.

The Angelicoussis Group, a privately owned group of affiliated shipping companies dating back to 1947, operates a diversified fleet serving the oil, gas and dry cargo markets through Athens-based companies, Maran Tankers Management (MTM), Maran Gas Maritime (MGM) and Maran Dry Management (MDM), and Maran Shuttle Tankers (MST), based in Stavanger, Norway.
To remind, Maran Gas Maritime was established in 2003 to undertake the commercial, technical and operational management of LNG carriers.

sum: The Dollar Index is drastically reversing (USDIDX: -0.6%) in reaction to Donald Trump's declaration that he has ordered the postponement of all attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure for the next five days. In his statement, the US president added that over the past two days, both sides of the conflict have held productive discussions regarding a potential halt to operations.
The USDIDX was close to erasing all of its losses from last Thursday, but Trump's statement halted the strong safe-haven flight to the dollar. Source: xStation5

Trump's declaration pivoted the markets from broad and deep declines to a global rebound. The relief of stress regarding a deeper escalation—and fears of even greater disruption to global energy supply chains—instantly dispelled risk aversion, turning most indices green.

- European Indices: Futures on the German DAX (DE40: +2.7%), which had remained the most exposed to the negative beta of the energy sector, are bouncing back the strongest. The broad EU50 gains around 2.3%, while Polish W20 adds a more modest 0.5%, still weighed down by a 4% drop in Orlen shares.
- Banks are recording the largest gains, as their financial results remain sensitive to general economic trends (PKO BP: +4%, HSBC, UniCredit: +3.8%).
- Energy companies flashed red, following the sudden slump in oil prices (Shell: -3.5%, BP: -4.1%, Orlen: -4%).

- Currency Market: A sharp reversal occurred on the dollar. The British pound became the biggest beneficiary of the relief (GBPUSD: +0.5%, GBPCHF: +0.55%), having been hit hard by the recent sell-off in UK bonds. EURUSD is gaining 0.2% to 1.158. Meanwhile, risk-sensitive Antipodean currencies (AUDUSD, NZDUSD) are up by a mere 0.2%, which may underscore the lack of any real improvement in the global economic outlook given the still-closed Strait of Hormuz.

items.t: Energy Min obliges Orlen Lietuva to release 80,000 tonnes of fuel reserves
sum: The International Energy Agency (IEA) authorised the member states to release a part of national fuel reserves to the market due to oil price spike amid the conflict in the Middle East.
Countries were allowed to supply to the market a total of 400 million barrels of oil and oil product reserves.
The topic was discussed at a meeting on Tuesday in which representatives of the Lithuanian Energy Agency, responsible for administering state reserves, and Orlen Lietuva participated.

The Ministry of Energy stressed that the security of oil and fuel supply has been ensured in the Baltic States, but fluctuations in global markets have a direct impact on prices in the region. Therefore, collective action taken on the international level is crucial for safeguarding consumers and the economy against prices hikes and for creating conditions for price stabilisation.
Lithuania’s fuel reserves total 650,000 tonnes. 60-day reserves are accumulated by fuel suppliers, whereas the state accumulates 30-day reserves.

items.t: ORLEN Neptun selects Polish companies for Baltic East FEED
sum: The works will include the preparation of comprehensive technical documentation and a detailed cost estimate for the investment, which will enable precise planning of further stages of the project. These measures will also significantly reduce the risks associated with potential delays and unforeseen cost increases during the construction of the farm.

Studies will aim for the 900 MW Baltic East offshore wind farm with the potential to provide clean energy to more than 1 million households. This is an important step towards increasing the share of renewable energy sources in the Polish energy mix and strengthening national energy independence.

Numerous Polish entities will be engaged in the process, including Geofizyka Torun S.A., archeological company Glesum, Maritime University of Szczecin, the National Institute of Telecommunications, Polish Naval Academy, Squadron Sp. z o.o., and ASE Offshore Sp. z o.o. The participation of domestic companies and scientific institutions not only strengthens their position in the offshore wind sector, but also contributes to building competences and developing technology for energy transition in Poland.

“When implementing strategic investments, we strive to make use of the potential of Polish companies, and their participation at the farm design stage is a clear indication that, thanks to the experience gained in the first phase of offshore wind power industry development, the domestic market is increasingly ready to invest in the rapidly growing offshore wind power sector. The formation of a domestic supply chain is a joint effort by suppliers, investors, public institutions and industry organisa-tions, as well as measures taken by the government, which are already showing their first results,” said Janusz Bil, President of the Management Board of ORLEN Neptun.

The works performed as part of FEED are a crucial engineering stage preceding the start of the actual construction works of the offshore wind farm. The project consortium will carry out detailed analyses of geotechnical, hydrological, and wind conditions at the chosen location, and will also develop technical specifications for turbines, foundations, substations, and offshore wind cable infrastructure.

items.t: Poland’s Orlen reports €2.6 bln profit for 2025 [VIDEO]
sum: The group also posted more than €63 billion in revenue for the year. Orlen’s CEO said the company reduced its debt in 2025 while investing over €7.5 billion, with a significant share of that spending going to Polish firms. Orlen is expanding across oil and gas production, petrochemicals and power, including renewable energy projects. The group operates refineries in Poland, the Czech Republic and Lithuania, and runs a network of service stations in Poland, Germany, Czechia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Hungary and Austria.
